status: Candidates for human review. Nothing here is in data/taxonomy.json.
rules: camel_case: mixed case inside the word, e.g. FastAPI, LangChain.
tech_style: dot or digits in tech style (Next.js, k8s, gpt-4o), or ends with ++ or #.
all_caps: 2 to 6 capital letters, unless in data/discover_stoplist.txt.
list: a single word in a comma/slash list with >= 2 different taxonomy skills (strongest signal).
Rules camel_case, tech_style and all_caps ignore the header cell (text before the first '|').
Terms in the taxonomy (pattern, name or synonym) and in the stoplist are dropped.
A term needs >= 30 posts in the last 12 months, and >= 50% of them must show it in rule style.
growth = share_last / max(share_prior, 1 / n_prior_posts). share = posts with the term / all posts in the 12 months.
score = growth x (0.5 + 0.5 x list_fraction). list_fraction = posts where the term is in a skill list / posts with the term. Terms with no posts in the prior 12 months are 'new'.
label = existing Welch test (engine.forecast.trend_label): last 12 months vs the 12 before.
co-occurring skills = top 3 taxonomy skills by lift in the last 12 months (>= 5 shared posts).

backfill_demo.note: Monthly share from the raw posts with the draft pattern: the history an approved skill gets at once.

backtest.definition: Run discover with data up to 2023-06. Take the top 15. A hit is a term whose share of posts in the next 12 months is above its share in the 12 months up to 2023-06. No month after as_of is used to choose the terms. The taxonomy and stoplist are today's files.
backtest.verdict: Weak: at most half of the top candidates grew.
caveats: Small sample: 15 terms. The interval is wide.
Compare with base_rate_all_candidates: a high precision is only informative if it beats the base rate.
The stoplist was written by reading today's candidates, not the 2023 ones, but it is human judgement.
